steps.message:
## Your budget

You have 5 minutes and 40 tool calls for this task. A grep costs about 5
seconds, a test run can cost 30. Call get_status to see what remains.

Spend at most a third of your budget locating the code. Once you have a
plausible diagnosis, edit the source — a wrong patch scores the same as no
patch, so an unverified fix always beats an unfinished investigation. If
get_status shows half your time gone and you have not yet edited a source
file, stop investigating and make your best edit now.

## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Edit the source first. Only write a reproduction script once you have made
your edit and submitted it, and only if budget remains to run it.

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — everything left
in /workspace becomes your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py or
pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

The harness truncates what you receive: 5,000 characters from any command,
and 150 lines or 10,000 characters from read_file. A truncated result loses
information silently, so a broad read wastes a call AND leaves you guessing.

Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Then read_file with a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole
file and never cat one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

    """Construct a Syntax object to render syntax highlighted code.

    Args:
        code (str): Code to highlight.
        lexer (Lexer | str): Lexer to use (see https://pygments.org/docs/lexers/)
        theme (str, optional): Color theme, aka Pygments style (see https://pygments.org/docs/styles/#getting-a-list-of-available-styles). Defaults to "monokai".
        dedent (bool, optional): Enable stripping of initial whitespace. Defaults to False.
        line_numbers (bool, optional): Enable rendering of line numbers. Defaults to False.
        start_line (int, optional): Starting number for line numbers. Defaults to 1.
        line_range (Tuple[int | None, int | None], optional): If given should be a tuple of the start and end line to render.
            A value of None in the tuple indicates the range is open in that direction.
        highlight_lines (Set[int]): A set of line numbers to highlight.
        code_width: Width of code to render (not including line numbers), or ``None`` to use all available width.
        tab_size (int, optional): Size of tabs. Defaults to 4.
        word_wrap (bool, optional): Enable word wrapping.
        background_color (str, optional): Optional background color, or None to use theme color. Defaults to None.
        indent_guides (bool, optional): Show indent guides. Defaults to False.
        padding (PaddingDimensions): Padding to apply around the syntax. Defaults to 0 (no padding).
    """

    _pygments_style_class: Type[PygmentsStyle]
    _theme: SyntaxTheme

    @classmethod
    def get_theme(cls, name: Union[str, SyntaxTheme]) -> SyntaxTheme:
        """Get a syntax theme instance."""
        if isinstance(name, SyntaxTheme):
            return name
        theme: SyntaxTheme
        if name in RICH_SYNTAX_THEMES:
            theme = ANSISyntaxTheme(RICH_SYNTAX_THEMES[name])
        else:
            theme = PygmentsSyntaxTheme(name)
        return theme

    def __init__(
        self,
        code: str,
        lexer: Union[Lexer, str],
        *,
        theme: Union[str, SyntaxTheme] = DEFAULT_THEME,
        dedent: bool = False,
        line_numbers: bool = False,
        start_line: int = 1,
        line_range: Optional[Tuple[Optional[int], Optional[int]]] = None,
        highlight_lines: Optional[Set[int]] = None,
        code_width: Optional[int] = None,
        tab_size: int = 4,
        word_wrap: bool = False,
        background_color: Optional[str] = None,
        indent_guides: bool = False,
        padding: PaddingDimensions = 0,
    ) -> None:
        self.code = code
        self._lexer = lexer
        self.dedent = dedent
        self.line_numbers = line_numbers
        self.start_line = start_line
        self.line_range = line_range
        self.highlight_lines = highlight_lines or set()
        self.code_width = code_width
        self.tab_size = tab_size
        self.word_wrap = word_wrap
        self.background_color = background_color
        self.background_style = (
            Style(bgcolor=background_color) if background_color else Style()
        )
        self.indent_guides = indent_guides
        self.padding = padding

        self._theme = self.get_theme(theme)
        self._stylized_ranges: List[_SyntaxHighlightRange] = []

    @classmethod
    def from_path(
        cls,
        path: str,
        encoding: str = "utf-8",
        lexer: Optional[Union[Lexer, str]] = None,
        theme: Union[str, SyntaxTheme] = DEFAULT_THEME,
        dedent: bool = False,
        line_numbers: bool = False,
        line_range: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None,
        start_line: int = 1,
        highlight_lines: Optional[Set[int]] = None,
        code_width: Optional[int] = None,
        tab_size: int = 4,
        word_wrap: bool = False,
        background_color: Optional[str] = None,
        indent_guides: bool = False,
        padding: PaddingDimensions = 0,
    ) -> "Syntax":
        """Construct a Syntax object from a file.

        Args:
            path (str): Path to file to highlight.
            encoding (str): Encoding of file.
            lexer (str | Lexer, optional): Lexer to use. If None, lexer will be auto-detected from path/file content.
            theme (str, optional): Color theme, aka Pygments style (see https://pygments.org/docs/styles/#getting-a-list-of-available-styles). Defaults to "emacs".
            dedent (bool, optional): Enable stripping of initial whitespace. Defaults to True.
            line_numbers (bool, optional): Enable rendering of line numbers. Defaults to False.
            start_line (int, optional): Starting number for line numbers. Defaults to 1.
            line_range (Tuple[int, int], optional): If given should be a tuple of the start and end line to render.
            highlight_lines (Set[int]): A set of line numbers to highlight.
            code_width: Width of code to render (not including line numbers), or ``None`` to use all available width.
            tab_size (int, optional): Size of tabs. Defaults to 4.
            word_wrap (bool, optional): Enable word wrapping of code.
            background_color (str, optional): Optional background color, or None to use theme color. Defaults to None.

            padding (PaddingDimensions): Padding to apply around the syntax. Defaults to 0 (no padding).

        Returns:
            [Syntax]: A Syntax object that may be printed to the console
